es.summary: Síndrome de desgaste corporal caracterizado por pérdida de masa muscular y grasa en pacientes con enfermedades crónicas avanzadas.
key_points: Pérdida involuntaria de >5% del peso corporal en 6 meses.
Inflamación crónica y alteración del metabolismo proteico son la base fisiopatológica.
Frecuente en cáncer avanzado, EPOC severa, insuficiencia cardíaca y VIH.
Aumenta el riesgo de infección, caídas y mortalidad.

pathophysiology: Inflamación sistémica libera citocinas (TNF‑α, IL‑6) que aumentan el catabolismo proteico.
Disminución de la síntesis de proteínas y aumento de la degradación muscular.
Alteración del eje hipotálamo‑hipófiso‑suprarrenal reduce el apetito.
Hipermetabolismo y resistencia a la insulina favorecen la pérdida de grasa.
risk_factors: Cáncer avanzado, especialmente de páncreas, pulmón y estómago.
Insuficiencia cardíaca congestiva y enfermedad renal crónica.
Desnutrición previa, anorexia y uso prolongado de corticoides.
signs_symptoms: Pérdida de peso involuntaria >5% en 6‑12 meses.
Atrofia muscular visible, debilidad y fatiga.
diagnostics: Peso y % de pérdida de peso registrado semanalmente.
Índice de masa corporal (IMC) <20 kg/m² o <22 en pacientes mayores.
Análisis de sangre: albúmina <3.5 g/dL, proteína total baja, PCR elevada.
Electrolitos y glucosa para descartar desequilibrios metabólicos.
treatment: Optimizar ingesta calórica: dietas hipercalóricas y altas en proteína.
Suplementos orales de proteína y ácidos grasos esenciales.
Control de la enfermedad subyacente (quimioterapia, terapia broncodilatadora).
Farmacoterapia antiinflamatoria (p. ej., inhibidores de la IL‑6) según indicación.
complications: Inmunosupresión y mayor riesgo de infecciones.
Debilidad respiratoria que puede precipitar insuficiencia respiratoria.
Caídas y fracturas por pérdida de masa muscular.
nursing_care: Monitorear peso diario y registrar tendencia.
Evaluar ingesta calórica y composición de macronutrientes cada turno.
Controlar signos de deshidratación y edema.
Colaborar con nutricionista para plan de alimentación individualizado.
Vigilar laboratorios de albúmina, electrolitos y glucosa.
patient_teaching: Explicar la importancia de comidas pequeñas y frecuentes con alto contenido calórico.
Enseñar técnicas para mejorar el apetito (ej. alimentos aromáticos, evitar olores fuertes).
Promover actividad física ligera para preservar masa muscular.
Instruir sobre signos de deshidratación y cuándo buscar ayuda médica.

evidenced_by: disminución de la tolerancia al ejercicio
outcomes: Nivel de energía: Aumento del nivel de energía a 3‑4 en escala de 0‑5
Capacidad de actividad: Realizar actividades de la vida diaria con mínima ayuda

interventions.rationale: Permite cuantificar la intolerancia y ajustar el plan de cuidados

interventions.action: Planificar períodos de descanso programado entre actividades
interventions.rationale: Reduce la sobrecarga muscular y mejora la tolerancia

interventions.action: Fomentar ejercicios de resistencia ligera bajo supervisión
interventions.rationale: Mantiene masa muscular y mejora la capacidad funcional

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta calórica y ofrecer suplementos proteicos
interventions.rationale: Apoya la energía necesaria para la actividad

interventions.action: Colaborar con fisioterapeuta para diseñar programa de movilización gradual
interventions.rationale: Optimiza la recuperación de la fuerza sin provocar agotamiento

Balance hídrico: Registro de entrada y salida con diferencia <+500 mL/24h

interventions.rationale: Detecta cambios tempranos en el estado de líquidos

interventions.rationale: Permite intervención oportuna

en.summary: Body wasting syndrome characterized by loss of muscle and fat mass in patients with advanced chronic illnesses.
key_points: Unintentional loss of >5% of body weight in 6 months.
Chronic inflammation and altered protein metabolism are the pathophysiological basis.
Common in advanced cancer, severe COPD, heart failure, and HIV.
Increases risk of infection, falls, and mortality.

pathophysiology: Systemic inflammation releases cytokines (TNF‑α, IL‑6) that increase protein catabolism.
Decreased protein synthesis and increased muscle degradation.
Alteration of the hypothalamic‑pituitary‑adrenal axis reduces appetite.
Hypermetabolism and insulin resistance favor fat loss.
risk_factors: Advanced cancer, especially pancreas, lung, and stomach.
Congestive heart failure and chronic kidney disease.
Prior malnutrition, anorexia, and prolonged steroid use.
signs_symptoms: Visible muscle atrophy, weakness, and fatigue.
diagnostics: Weight and % weight loss recorded weekly.
Body mass index (BMI) <20 kg/m² or <22 in older adults.
Blood tests: albumin <3.5 g/dL, low total protein, elevated CRP.
Electrolytes and glucose to rule out metabolic imbalances.
treatment: Optimize caloric intake: hypercaloric and high‑protein diets.
Oral protein supplements and essential fatty acids.
Anti‑inflammatory pharmacotherapy (e.g., IL‑6 inhibitors) as indicated.
complications: Respiratory weakness that may precipitate respiratory failure.
Falls and fractures from muscle loss.
nursing_care: Monitor daily weight and record trends.
Assess caloric intake and macronutrient composition each shift.
Check for dehydration and edema signs.
Collaborate with dietitian for individualized nutrition plan.
Monitor labs for albumin, electrolytes, and glucose.
patient_teaching: Explain the importance of small, frequent high‑calorie meals.
Teach appetite‑enhancing techniques (e.g., aromatic foods, avoid strong odors).
Encourage light physical activity to preserve muscle mass.
Instruct on dehydration signs and when to seek medical help.

outcomes: Energy level: Increase energy level to 3‑4 on 0‑5 scale
Activity capacity: Perform activities of daily living with minimal assistance

interventions.action: Assess fatigue level using Borg scale each shift
interventions.rationale: Allows quantification of intolerance and adjustment of care plan

interventions.action: Plan scheduled rest periods between activities
interventions.rationale: Reduces muscle overload and improves tolerance

interventions.action: Encourage light resistance exercise under supervision
interventions.rationale: Maintains muscle mass and improves functional capacity

interventions.action: Record caloric intake and offer protein supplements
interventions.rationale: Supports necessary energy for activity

interventions.action: Collaborate with physiotherapist to design gradual mobilization program
interventions.rationale: Optimizes strength recovery without causing exhaustion

outcomes: Hydration status: Maintain adequate hydration with intake >30 mL/kg/day
Fluid balance: Record intake and output with difference <+500 mL/24h

interventions.action: Monitor daily weight and compare with fluid balance
interventions.rationale: Detect early changes in fluid status

interventions.action: Assess signs of dehydration (skin turgor, dry mucous membranes)
interventions.rationale: Allows timely intervention

interventions.action: Offer fluids between meals and record total intake
interventions.rationale: Ensures compliance with hydration requirements

interventions.action: Administer oral rehydration solutions as ordered
interventions.rationale: Corrects electrolyte and volume deficits

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of drinking at least 2 L of water daily
interventions.rationale: Promotes self‑care and dehydration prevention

summary.0.quote: Because of the increased effort required to breathe, patients with chronic COPD can develop muscle wasting and cachexia , a disorder that causes loss of muscle and adipose tissue ( Figure 11.20 ).

sections.signs_symptoms.3.quote: In advanced cases, right-sided heart failure can occur, causing lower extremity edema (Agarwal et al., 2023).

sections.treatment.0.quote: Sometimes a high-calorie, high-fat diet is a better option for a malnourished patient where every bite counts.

sections.complications.3.quote: It can cause chronic illness, hospitalization, and death.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Nutritionists to provide disease specific meal plans and supplements
